meta.title: Daily Reflection Tree
meta.description: An end-of-day deterministic reflection tool built on three psychological axes: Locus of Control, Contribution Orientation, and Radius of Concern.
meta.author: DT Fellowship Candidate

nodes.text: Good evening. Today happened — some of it as you planned, some of it not. This is a short conversation to help you make sense of it. No grades, no judgments. Just honest reflection. Ready when you are.
Let's start simply. If you had to describe today in one word, which feels most true?

options.label: Productive
Tough
Mixed
Frustrating

nodes.text: You said today felt '{A1_OPEN.value}'. When something went well, what do you think drove it?

options.label: I prepared and showed up ready
I adapted when things shifted
The team or timing worked in my favour
Honestly, I'm not sure — it just did

nodes.text: You said today felt '{A1_OPEN.value}'. When things got hard, what was your first instinct?

options.label: Look for what I could still control
Push through alone and hope it cleared
Wait for someone else to step in
Feel stuck, not sure what to do next

nodes.text: You seem to have stayed in the driver's seat today. Here's a more granular question: when a decision was in front of you, what guided you most?

options.label: My own judgment and experience
The reaction I expected from others
What the situation seemed to call for
I avoided making a call when I could

nodes.text: Think of one specific moment today when things felt out of your control. Looking back, was there any small choice available to you — even one you didn't take?

options.label: Yes, I can see it now
Maybe — I wasn't thinking that way in the moment
Not really — it was genuinely beyond me
I haven't thought about it that way before

nodes.text: You moved through today with a sense of agency — not control over everything, but ownership over how you responded. That's not a small thing. Most people react; fewer choose how to respond. Hold onto that.

Tough days pull our attention outward — to what others did or didn't do, to the luck of the situation. That's human. But somewhere in today, even once, you made a call. It might have been small. It counts. Tomorrow, that's worth watching for.
We've looked at how you moved through today. Now let's look at what you gave — and what you expected.
Think about your interactions today — with a colleague, a manager, a client, anyone. Which of these best fits a moment that stands out?

options.label: I helped someone with something outside my role
I felt my effort wasn't seen or credited
I did something extra without being asked
I felt others weren't carrying their share

nodes.text: You seem to have been in a giving mode today. What drove that — why did you give the extra effort?

options.label: It felt like the right thing to do
I was hoping it would be noticed
The other person genuinely needed it
I wasn't really thinking about it — habit

nodes.text: You mentioned feeling like something was missing — recognition, effort from others. When that feeling showed up, what did you do with it?

options.label: I let it go and focused on my work
I brought it up with the person involved
I held onto it — it's still bothering me
I pulled back my own effort in response

nodes.text: You were in contribution mode today. That kind of giving — especially when it's not tracked or rewarded — is exactly what builds trust on a team. People remember who showed up for them. You did that today.

There's nothing wrong with wanting your effort to be seen. That's a real human need. The question worth sitting with is: was today's attention mostly on what you received, or on what you gave? One of those energises a team. The other, quietly, doesn't.
One more lens. We've talked about your agency and your contribution. Now — how wide was your view today? Who else were you thinking about?
When you think about today's biggest challenge, who came to mind most naturally?

options.label: Just me — it was my problem to solve
My immediate team — we were all affected
A specific colleague who had a harder day than me
The people we're ultimately serving

nodes.text: You thought of others. Did that awareness change anything about how you acted today?

options.label: Yes — I adjusted what I was doing because of it
I thought about it but it didn't change my actions
I offered help or support to that person
Not really — I noted it and moved on

nodes.text: You were zoomed in on your own problem today — which is often necessary. But let's look around the edges: was there anyone near you who might have been struggling too, even if you didn't engage with it?

options.label: Yes, I noticed — I just didn't have capacity
Yes, and I realise I could have checked in
Not really — I was heads-down
I hadn't thought about it until now

nodes.text: You looked up from your own work today and saw who else was in the room. That's a wider radius than most people operate with, especially on hard days. The research is clear: people who connect their work to others' wellbeing find it more meaningful — and sustain it longer.

You were in your own world today — and sometimes that's exactly where you need to be. But meaning at work rarely lives there permanently. Tomorrow, try one small thing: notice one person's experience before your day ends. Not to fix it. Just to see it.

summary_reflections.internal_contribution_altrocentric: You brought agency, generosity, and a wide view today. On a hard day, that's harder than it sounds. This is worth protecting.
summary_reflections.internal_contribution_self_centric: You took ownership and gave effort today. The one gap: your view was mostly inward. Tomorrow, widen the frame just slightly.
summary_reflections.internal_entitlement_altrocentric: You moved with agency and saw others — but some of your energy went toward what you were owed rather than what you could give. Notice that gap.
summary_reflections.internal_entitlement_self_centric: Strong on ownership, but today's frame was narrow — your needs, your recognition, your outcomes. That's a starting point, not an ending point.
summary_reflections.external_contribution_altrocentric: You gave to others and thought beyond yourself today — even if you didn't feel fully in control. Contribution is its own kind of agency.
summary_reflections.external_contribution_self_centric: You gave effort today, which matters. The agency piece is still developing — but contribution is a genuine starting point.
summary_reflections.external_entitlement_self_centric: A tough day on every dimension. External, expecting, inward-facing. Be honest with yourself about whether this is a rough patch or a pattern.
summary_reflections.external_entitlement_altrocentric: You noticed others even when you were struggling yourself — that's real. The agency and entitlement pieces are worth returning to.

nodes.text: See you tomorrow. Same time, different day.
